meta.name: English
meta.title: Password365 — Not your server, not your passwords.
meta.description: Passwords, passkeys and one-time codes in an encrypted vault that stays on your devices. No account, no cloud: your computer and your phone sync directly.

hero.eyebrow: Synced across your devices. Stored on no one else's.
hero.title: Not your server, not your passwords.
hero.lead: Password365 keeps your passwords, passkeys and one-time codes in sync across your computer, phone and tablet — without ever putting them on a server you don't control. No account, no cloud.
hero.note: Free for Mac, Windows and Linux. iPhone and iPad coming soon.

why.title: Why not the cloud?
why.lead: Cloud password managers encrypt your vault too. But they keep it — and millions of others — on their servers.

target.title: One target, millions of vaults
target.text: A server holding everyone's encrypted vaults is worth attacking. When one is breached, attackers take the vaults with them and can keep guessing at the passwords for as long as they like.

control.title: Your copy, your rules
control.text: With Password365 your vault lives only on your devices, kept in sync between them. There is no copy on anyone else's server to steal, leak or lose access to.

offline.title: Works without the internet
offline.text: No outage, no lost account and no change of terms can lock you out of your own passwords.

why.quote: Crypto holders say: not your keys, not your coins. The same is true of passwords: if they live on someone else's server, they are only as safe as that server.

features.title: Everything a password manager should do
features.lead: The features you expect, on your own devices.

autofill.title: Fills in for you
autofill.text: Usernames, passwords and one-time codes filled in on websites and apps, from the browser extension and from AutoFill on iPhone and iPad.

passkeys.title: Passkeys
passkeys.text: Create and use passkeys on any site that supports them, and keep them with the rest of your logins.

totp.title: Two-factor codes built in
totp.text: Add the setup key once and Password365 shows the code, and fills it in together with your password.

watchtower.title: Watchtower
watchtower.text: Finds weak, reused and old passwords, and logins that could use two-factor authentication. Checked on your device.

categories.title: More than passwords
categories.text: Credit cards, identities, secure notes, bank accounts, passports, Wi-Fi, SSH keys, documents and more than 20 categories, with the right fields for your country.

generator.title: Strong passwords on demand
generator.text: Random passwords, easy-to-type passphrases and PINs, generated on the spot.

quickAccess.title: Quick Access
quickAccess.text: A keyboard shortcut opens your vault over any app on your computer: search, copy, done.

attachments.title: Files and documents
attachments.text: Attach scans and files to any item, encrypted like everything else.

ssh.title: For developers
ssh.text: An SSH agent for the keys in your vault, and auto-type for apps that do not accept filling.

sync.title: All your devices in sync. No cloud in between.
sync.lead: Not an offline vault you have to copy around: add as many computers, phones and tablets as you like and they keep each other up to date automatically. They talk directly, on your own network — your vault never goes through a server, ours or anyone else's.

step1.title: Pair once
step1.text: Scan a QR code shown on your computer with your iPhone. That is the whole setup.

step2.title: Change anywhere
step2.text: Add or edit items on any device. Each change is encrypted before it leaves the device.

step3.title: Stay in sync
step3.text: The next time both devices are on the same network, they exchange what changed. No account, no subscription to a cloud.

security.title: Encrypted before anything else happens
security.lead: Your vault is unlocked by two secrets: the master password you remember and a Secret Key that is created on your device and never leaves your hands.

keys.title: Two keys, not one
keys.text: Even someone with a copy of your vault file and a lucky guess at your password cannot open it without your Secret Key.

crypto.title: Modern, proven cryptography
crypto.text: Argon2id makes guessing your password slow and expensive. XChaCha20-Poly1305 encrypts and authenticates every item.

local.title: Nothing to breach
local.text: There is no central server holding everyone's vaults, so there is no central server to break into.

migrate.title: Bring your passwords with you
migrate.lead: Import from your browser or your current password manager in a few clicks. Logins, cards, notes, passkeys and attachments come along where the export includes them.
migrate.others: and CSV or CXF files from other apps

platforms.title: On the devices you use

faq.title: Questions
faq.q0: Is this an offline password manager where I copy the vault file myself?
faq.a0: No. Password365 syncs automatically between all your devices, like a cloud password manager does — the difference is that the devices talk to each other directly instead of through someone else's server. There are no files to move by hand.
faq.q1: What happens if I lose my phone?
faq.a1: Your vault is encrypted and locked with Face ID or Touch ID and your master password. Your items are still on your computer, and you can set up a new phone from it.
faq.q2: What if I forget my master password?
faq.a2: Nobody can reset it for you — that is what keeps your vault private. Keep your Emergency Kit (it has your Secret Key and room to write your password) somewhere safe, and back up your vault from the app.
faq.q3: Do I need to be on the same network to sync?
faq.a3: Yes. Devices sync when they can reach each other on the same network. In between, each device keeps working on its own with everything it has.
faq.q4: Does Password365 use the internet at all?
faq.a4: Only if you turn on the check for passwords found in data breaches (off by default). It sends the first 5 characters of a hash of each password, never the password itself.
faq.q5: Can I move my data out later?
faq.a5: Yes. Export everything to CSV or to the Credential Exchange Format (CXF), which other password managers can import, passkeys included.

cta.title: Take your passwords back.
cta.text: Free on your computer. No account needed.

download.title: Download Password365
download.lead: Start on your computer, then add your phone and your browser.
download.extensionText: For Chrome, Edge and Firefox. It works together with the app on your computer.
download.iosText: AutoFill, passkeys and Face ID, synced with your computer.

securityPage.title: Security
securityPage.lead: How Password365 protects your data, in plain words and in detail.
securityPage.p1: Your data is encrypted on your device before it is written anywhere.
securityPage.p2: Only you hold the keys. We never see your master password, your Secret Key or your items, and we cannot recover them.
securityPage.p3: Devices sync directly with each other. There is no Password365 server.
securityPage.p4: The only online features, the breached-password check and update checks, are off until you turn them on.
securityPage.unlock1: Your master password is stretched with Argon2id (256 MB of memory on computers, 128 MB on phones), which makes every guess slow and costly.
securityPage.unlock2: Your Secret Key — 128 random bits created on your device — is mixed in with HKDF-SHA-256. A copy of your vault cannot be attacked with password guesses alone.
securityPage.unlock3: After a few wrong passwords in a row, each new try has to wait longer.
securityPage.enc1: Every item is encrypted with XChaCha20-Poly1305, with a random nonce each time. Any change to the encrypted data is detected and refused.
securityPage.enc2: Each encrypted record is bound to its vault, its item and its version, so records cannot be swapped or replayed.
securityPage.enc3: On iPhone, the vault file also gets the system's file protection, and Face ID unlock keeps its key in the Secure Enclave–protected Keychain, for 14 days at most before your master password is needed again.
securityPage.sync1: Pairing uses a QR code shown on your computer: the phone and the computer authenticate each other with it before anything is exchanged.
securityPage.sync2: Every sync runs over an end-to-end encrypted channel (the Noise protocol with X25519), on your local network.
securityPage.sync3: A device can be removed from your account at any time.
securityPage.data2: If you turn on the breached-password check, the first 5 characters of the SHA-1 hash of each password are sent to Have I Been Pwned, which answers with every matching hash (k-anonymity). The password never leaves your device.
securityPage.open1: The cryptography is written down in a detailed specification, with test vectors, and checked by automated tests on every change.

privacyPage.title: Privacy policy
privacyPage.intro: Password365 is built so that we do not have your data. This policy explains what that means in practice.
privacyPage.apps1: Password365 does not collect any data. There is no account and no sign-up. Your vault is created, encrypted and kept on your devices.
privacyPage.apps2: Devices sync directly with each other on your local network. Your data does not pass through any server of ours.
privacyPage.apps3: The apps contain no analytics, no advertising and no tracking of any kind.
privacyPage.apps4: If you turn on the breached-password check (off by default), the app sends the first 5 characters of a hash of each password to Have I Been Pwned (haveibeenpwned.com). It cannot learn your passwords from them.
privacyPage.store1: Apps downloaded from the App Store are delivered by Apple, and any purchase is processed by Apple under its own privacy policy. We do not receive your payment details.
privacyPage.site1: This website uses no cookies and no analytics. It is served by Cloudflare, which processes technical data such as IP addresses to deliver and protect it.
privacyPage.apps5: If you turn on update checks (the app asks the first time you open it), the desktop app asks GitHub (github.com), where Password365 is published, for the newest version once a day. GitHub sees the request, like any website visit; nothing about you or your vault is sent.

supportPage.title: Support
supportPage.contact: Write to {email}. Never send us your master password or your Secret Key — we will never ask for them.
supportPage.start1: Install Password365 on your computer and create your vault. Save the Emergency Kit it offers: it holds your Secret Key.
supportPage.start2: Import your passwords from your browser or your current password manager (Import, in the toolbar).
supportPage.start3: Install the browser extension to fill in and save logins.
supportPage.start4: On your iPhone, choose “Set up with another device” and scan the QR code shown on your computer, in Devices.
supportPage.recover1: You need your master password and your Secret Key. The Secret Key is on your Emergency Kit, and in Settings on any device that is still signed in.
supportPage.recover2: Nobody, including us, can reset your master password.

footer.tagline: The password manager without a cloud.

open.title: Open source, checked in the open
open.lead: You should not have to take our word for it. All of Password365's code is public, so anyone can read it, build it and check what it does with your passwords.

code.title: Read the code
code.text: The apps, the browser extension and the cryptography are published on GitHub under the GPL-3.0 license: free to use, study and share.

verify.title: Verify it
verify.text: The cryptography and the sync protocol are written down, with a threat model. Automated tests run on every change. It has not had an independent audit yet; we say so, and we welcome reviewers.

help.title: Help build it
help.text: Report a bug, suggest an idea, add your language or send a fix. Found a vulnerability? Report it privately and we will answer within 7 days.
